brief: A single hex base, nothing else added beside or on top of it, with five drawers in it.

requirements.requirement: Single hex base with nothing added beside or on top (single cell at level 0, no neighbors)
requirements.evidence: Build has one piece only: piece:0,0,0;half-n at 0,0,0. get_build shows counts piece:1, no other cells at level 0 adjacent and no level 1 piece. check_build confirms no adjacency.

Configurator offers max 1 drawer per single base: find_sockets drawer on half-n returned only 1 socket s40 (key 's'), on half-s 1 socket, on full/quarter 0 sockets. After placing 1 drawer (drawer:0#0,0#cut) no further drawer sockets offered. Five drawers is not offered by the system for a single isolated base - this is a system limit, not a placement error. Current build has 1/5 drawers.

finish.summary: Single isolated base cannot hold five drawers in the Hex Cluster configurator. A full base offers 0 drawer sockets, a half base offers 1, quarters offer 0. The build was set to half-n to demonstrate the max (1 drawer placed), but 5 is impossible without adding adjacent cells/notch/bay which would violate the 'nothing beside or on top' rule.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
